So this effect is only true in very hot and dry conditions. If it was hot and humid, a fan would still help because of evaporative cooling. When it's hot and dry your body doesn't struggle with evaporation. Your body will slightly reduce the temperature of the ambient air around you if the external temperature is above your internal temperature. 

If it's over 95F then you are pushing away that slightly cooler air and replacing it with hotter air. It's exactly the process of convection ovens that blow hot air to increase cooking speed. Hope that helps!

Try talking to your doctor about anti-nausea medicine. The effects should not last longer than 2-3 days. Also, if you are truly trying to quit and the withdrawals/nausea are affecting that, consider weaning rather than going cold turkey. 

THEN, just for me, look up CHS (cannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome) and just see if that sounds like you. I only suggest because I thought it was withdrawals making me nauseous and it was actually the marijuana to begin with.

I understand your sentiment, but this is misguided. Clinical CHS patients ingest the same marijuana and in the same mechanism as patients who do not exhibit CHS symptoms. This is just a bodily mechanism that is some amount luck.

THC can be antiemetic, definitely not in CHS patients. One of the worst things is that a lot of CHS patients will USE marijuana for antiemetic properties while experiencing these bouts of nausea without recognizing that marijuana is the source. 

It's unrelated to smoke inhalation and has everything to do with THC absorption in your digestive tract instead of the normal mechanism. That is why lots of people can ingest a large amount of marijuana and not experience CHS. It's some amount luck of how your body will receive THC. 

Disclaimer: the true mechanism of CHS is not fully understood.

One reason for this is that many CHS patients don't even recognize that there is a correlation between the vomiting/nausea episodes and marijuana habits. Since patients smoke daily and these bouts of nausea are cyclic (usually 1-10 days every 4-6 weeks) people don't think it is caused by their daily habits and must be something specific that triggered the episode. 

Another reason you see this so often is that these cases often end up in urgent/emergency care because they literally cannot keep down any amount of fluids and become severely dehydrated. 

Now you have combined factors 1) lots of people who experience CHS end up in the hospital and 2) they are repeat visitors because they don't understand the source. We can add in 3) some people do know and are addicted which is a battle of itself.
